scope: Read-only source comparison and isolated HTTP spike; no shipping behavior changed.

currentClientInspected.scope: Local source; this is not a claim about every installed BEX version.

findings: The REST listener remains up when the device locks in both releases and current develop; listener shutdown follows API setting changes or application exit.
Health and existing pairing remain available. Known-locked seed-dependent requests return HTTP 423.
The requireWallet lock check and top-level app phase resolver are byte-identical across all three refs.
Address and pubkey-batch routes call requireWallet before their cache lookup, so even correctly scoped warm caches are blocked while locked.
Needs-PIN eagerly prompts and replaces the main app with splash in both releases and develop; the setup default auto-lock remains one hour.
Develop protects active PIN/passphrase input from unrelated transport writes and stray acknowledgments. Preserve these guards.
A request already admitted before firmware reports a lock can continue after PIN entry; one started after known-lock receives 423 and is not automatically resumed.
Current BEX cold initialization without cached pubkeys can convert batch-pubkey failure into its errored state, despite the API remaining reachable.
Current BEX foreground EVM connect/message-sign flows read the address again; these can fail with 423. Signing has no dedicated unlock/resume contract.

Get-features is allowed during ordinary lock. With no usable snapshot while an input wait is active, the new transport input guard can refuse a live feature read; this does not stop the API or invalidate pairing.
recommendedContract: Represent API reachability, pairing validity, device presence, device lock and operation status separately.
Keep an already verified same-wallet portfolio and scoped public caches available while the device is locked; maintain setup and hidden-wallet privacy boundaries.
Background health, balance and metadata polling must not start PIN prompts.
Deliberate device operations enter one serialized, cancellable coordinator above transport, foreground Vault and await unlock once.
After unlock, revalidate wallet/device/session and quote freshness, then continue only the exact authorized request. Never blindly replay signing or broadcast.
On rejection, timeout, disconnect or wallet/passphrase change, return an explicit terminal result and clear that pending operation.
Keep transport PIN/passphrase/wipe ownership guards. Do not globally mark routes whileLocked or remove low-level checks.
Give BEX a locked/awaiting-unlock state that preserves pairing and cached data rather than calling a reachable Vault offline.
implementationOrder: Separate BEX liveness/readiness states and stop using a pubkey failure as evidence the API is offline.
Permit safe cache reads before the device-unlocked gate and preserve verified portfolio UI on device lock.
Implement a shared device-operation unlock coordinator and foreground prompt; update callers to wait/resume with cancellation and session fences.
Replace eager lock-state PIN prompting with demand-driven prompting after every sensitive caller uses the coordinator.
